nodes.content: Enable mobile manipulators to distinguish object slip from localization drift while maintaining contact during furniture repositioning.
requirements: Reposition unseen furniture within 5 cm in 90% of trials with intermittent visual occlusion.
Identify slip versus localization drift with 90% balanced accuracy without external tracking during execution.

nodes.content: Use contact-constrained factor-graph fusion of wrist shear, odometry, and intermittent RGB-D to distinguish slip from drift during furniture repositioning.
During three-second visual occlusions, which wrist-shear and contact-kinematic cues distinguish gripper slip from base-pose drift?
During three-second occlusions, contact residuals with shear spikes indicate slip; residuals without spikes indicate drift at ≥90% balanced accuracy.
Record FurnitureContact-1 with induced grip slip and odometry drift during three-second occlusions; fit shear-conditioned residuals and evaluate balanced accuracy.
Run FurnitureContact-1 held-out slip-versus-drift trials with three-second occlusions; compute balanced accuracy from wrist-shear-conditioned contact residuals.
On 120 held-out FurnitureContact-1 trials with three-second occlusions, shear-conditioned residuals classified slip versus drift at 92% balanced accuracy.
Analyze misclassifications from FurnitureContact-1’s 92% classifier, refit residuals on training trials, and reassess three-second-occlusion balanced accuracy.
FurnitureContact-1 diagnostic package containing labeled misclassifications, refitted shear-conditioned residual parameters, and held-out three-second-occlusion confusion matrices.
Audit diagnostic-package matrices; test refitted contact-graph fusion on tracker-free, occluded unseen-furniture trials for 5-cm success and slip/drift balanced accuracy.
On 100 tracker-free unseen-furniture trials, contact-graph fusion achieved 76% within 5 cm and 84% slip/drift balanced accuracy.
Defer contact-graph fusion deployment: tracker-free trials missed both 90% thresholds, achieving 76% placement success and 84% balanced accuracy.
Do caster-swivel transients mimic gripper slip during occlusion, contributing to the 84% tracker-free balanced accuracy?
Reanalyze 100 tracker-free trials, comparing slip false-positive rates during caster-swivel torque transients versus matched steady-motion intervals.
Tracker-free three-second-occlusion subset achieved 91% balanced accuracy versus 84% overall; swivel transients raised slip false positives from 5% to 14%.
Use caster-aware contact factors and low-force probing to separate slip from drift, correcting furniture pose with reacquired RGB-D.
Fit caster-aware factors, probe ambiguous shear at 8 N, and reacquire RGB-D; measure tracker-free 5-cm placement and slip/drift balanced accuracy.
Use FurnitureContact-1 diagnostic misclassifications to fit caster-swivel contact factors and calibrate 8 N probing triggers on training trials.
CasterFactor-v1 contains fitted swivel-contact residuals and 8 N ambiguity-trigger calibration derived from FurnitureContact-1 training trials.
Does CasterFactor-v1’s 8 N probe reduce swivel-induced slip false positives below 5% without moving furniture over 1 cm?
CasterFactor-v1’s 8 N reversal probe reduces swivel-induced slip false positives below 5%, with furniture displacement under 1 cm.
Test CasterFactor-v1’s 8 N probe on 60 held-out swivel trials; compare slip false positives and furniture displacement with controls.
On 60 held-out swivel trials, probing reduced slip false positives from 14% to 4%, but median displacement reached 1.6 cm.
Test CasterFactor-v1’s 8 N probe on 40 occluded, low-friction furniture trials; measure slip false positives and displacement.
On 40 occluded low-friction trials, CasterFactor-v1 yielded 2.5% slip false positives and 0.8 cm median probe displacement.
Can caster-state-dependent probe duration keep displacement below 1 cm across furniture types without raising slip false positives?
Use 1.6-cm swivel and 0.8-cm low-friction displacement results to tune caster-dependent probe durations; test 1-cm displacement and 5% false-positive limits.
Tune CasterFactor-v1’s 8 N probe duration by inferred caster state, targeting a 1 cm displacement budget on training furniture.
CasterFactor-v2 revises CasterFactor-v1 with 80 ms swivel and 140 ms low-friction 8 N probes targeting under 1 cm displacement.
Run 100 tracker-free occluded unseen-furniture trials with CasterFactor-v2 and RGB-D reacquisition; measure 5-cm placement, slip/drift balanced accuracy, probe displacement.
In 100 occluded tracker-free unseen-furniture trials, CasterFactor-v2 achieved 92% 5-cm placement, 91% slip/drift balanced accuracy, and 0.7-cm median probe displacement.
Fuse dual-gripper tactile motion with onboard lidar wall landmarks; correct grip slip or base drift while preserving contact.
Can onboard lidar distinguish simultaneous two-gripper slip from base drift when only one wall segment remains visible?
One-wall lidar innovations plus dual-gripper tactile velocities distinguish simultaneous slip from base drift at ≥90% balanced accuracy.
Run 100 tracker-free one-wall trials inducing simultaneous gripper slip or base drift; measure lidar-tactile balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
Across 100 tracker-free one-wall trials, lidar-tactile fusion achieved 83% balanced accuracy and 81% within-5-cm placement.
Test lidar-tactile fusion on 80 tracker-free two-wall trials with simultaneous slip; measure balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
Across 80 tracker-free two-wall slip/drift trials, lidar-tactile fusion achieved 92% balanced accuracy and 91% within-5-cm placement.
Can contact-preserving lidar viewpoint changes reveal a second wall landmark in one-wall scenes while limiting furniture displacement to 1 cm?
Use the one-wall versus two-wall performance gap to plan contact-preserving lidar sidesteps; test second-wall visibility and ≤1 cm displacement.
Using prior one-/two-wall benchmarks, test contact-preserving lidar sidesteps; record second-wall visibility, displacement, and one-wall pre-sidestep versus post-sidestep balanced accuracy.
Sidesteps revealed second walls in 38/60 trials; 22 remaining one-wall trials reached 91% balanced accuracy, with 0.8-cm median displacement.
Use lidar-tactile fusion as a two-wall auxiliary: 91% placement versus 81% one-wall; sidestep classification lacks placement validation.
Fuse gripper tactile optical flow with downward-facing floor-flow odometry to distinguish slip from drift and correct unseen furniture pose.
Calibrate floor-flow odometry and gripper tactile flow, then test slip/drift balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement on tracker-free occluded furniture.
Use CasterFactor-v2’s bounded probes to label training slip events; calibrate synchronized gripper tactile flow against downward floor-flow odometry.
FloorTactile-v1 contains synchronized 30 Hz floor-flow and gripper-flow calibration plus probe-labeled slip training events.
Run FloorTactile-v1 on 100 tracker-free, occluded unseen-furniture trials across tile and carpet; measure slip/drift balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement.
Across 100 tracker-free tile/carpet trials, FloorTactile-v1 achieved 93% within-5-cm placement and 92% slip/drift balanced accuracy.
Does FloorTactile-v1 retain ≥90% slip/drift balanced accuracy on glossy or textureless floors where downward optical flow degrades?
On glossy or textureless floors with fewer than 20 floor-flow tracks/frame, FloorTactile-v1 falls below 90% slip/drift balanced accuracy.
Test FloorTactile-v1 on glossy and textureless floors, stratifying tracker-free slip/drift balanced accuracy by 20 floor-flow tracks/frame.
Run 80 tracker-free glossy/textureless-floor trials with FloorTactile-v1; report balanced accuracy and 5-cm placement by floor-flow track count.
Among 44/80 glossy/textureless-floor trials with fewer than 20 tracks/frame, FloorTactile-v1 achieved 78% balanced accuracy and 82% within-5-cm placement.
Compare FloorTactile-v1 slip/drift balanced accuracy in 36 ≥20-track glossy/textureless trials against 44 documented low-track trials.
Glossy-floor trials retained 92% balanced accuracy below 20 tracks/frame versus 93% above; textureless cases drove the pooled 78%.
Which textureless-floor failure mode explains 78% pooled balanced accuracy despite 92% accuracy on low-track glossy floors?
Textureless floors concentrate tracks within one image quadrant, biasing odometry and lowering balanced accuracy below 80% regardless of track count.
Reanalyze discrepant glossy and textureless trials, stratifying floor-flow quadrant occupancy and odometry bias against slip/drift balanced accuracy.
Measure quadrant concentration, odometry bias, and slip/drift balanced accuracy across 80 glossy/textureless FloorTactile-v1 trials, controlling for track count.
Textureless trials with ≥75% single-quadrant tracks showed 4.2 cm/m odometry bias and 76% balanced accuracy across track-count strata.
Retain FloorTactile-v1 for tile/carpet; prioritize CasterFactor-v2 fallback for ≥75%-quadrant textureless flow, not low-track glossy scenes.
